subject: economics
title: AD, AS and the Multiplier
welcome_lead: Aggregate demand, aggregate supply and the multiplier explain output.
meta_desc: A-Level Macroeconomics: AD, AS, the multiplier.
final_note: Output equilibrium sits where AD meets AS - shocks shift both.

concepts.def: C + I + G + (X - M) - total spending in the economy.
Total output firms supply at each price level.
1 / (1 - MPC) - how an injection multiplies through spending.
Marginal propensity to consume out of extra income.
Difference between actual and potential output.
Output when all resources are fully employed.

walkthroughs.body_html: The AD curve shows total spending at each price level. Components are Consumption, Investment, Government spending and net X minus M exports.
SRAS slopes up because wages and contracts adjust slowly. LRAS is vertical at full employment - long run, only supply-side reforms shift it.
An extra 100 pounds of government spending becomes income for the receiver, who spends MPC of it, and so on. With MPC = 0.5, the multiplier is 1 / 0.5 = 2.
